newsitem.title: USA: Minn. Gov announces $120 mln flood recovery plan.
newsitem.headline: Minn. Gov announces $120 mln flood recovery plan.

text.p: Minnesota Gov. Arne Carlson announced that nearly $120 million from federal, state and private sources was committed to communities hit by massive flooding in April.
Carlson also plans to hold a special session in late summer to address additional funding needs that will likely involve the issuance of debt, a spokesman said Tuesday.
State and private sources will contribute $70 million toward rebuilding efforts and the federal disaster bill will provide another $50 million, Carlson said in a statement released Friday.
The state contribution will come from a combination of funds already allocated by lawmakers and reallocation of money budgeted for other uses, spokesman Patrick McCarthy said.

A state task force has been coordinating aid requests from the more than 400 Minnesota communities eligible for assistance and Carlson plans to call a special session in late August or September to address other immediate funding needs.
McCarthy said the community requests have reached $700 million for public needs alone, but accurate damage assessments have not been completed yet.

The federal government will fund the bulk of the repairs through a matching disaster relief funding program, McCarthy said. Minnesota will likely issue debt for the state and local share of that matching program, he said.

At this point, the federal government will fund 75 percent of the repairs and Minnesota 25 percent, McCarthy said. State officials would like that ratio to rise to 90 percent federal to 10 percent state and are still negotiating that point, he said.
